review_response_tasks.rationale: One branch of path与the other组成岔路分支对照。exception例外、shelter遮蔽处、transit运输不指路的分支；estimate虽可作名词，但路的一个估计不通；其他项不作此处路支名词。
letters had faded until almost nothing可读，指褪色。reversed若反转不会令颜料几乎不可见，后文反转另属手机照片；其余动词estimate/explore/identify/reach为原形，不能置于had后作完成式分词；其余项不表示褪色完成动作。
reach the village接到达地点与五点会面截止。identify识别村庄不实现去唯一车站会面；explore探索不等在截止前到达；estimate估计不以村庄作此数值对象；其他项不表示到达目的地。
offered shelter from shower表示提供避雨遮蔽。branch分支、exception例外、estimate估计、transit运输均不是抵御阵雨的保护；其余项不作此不可数保护名词。
river对边且tiny words mirror images明确reversed左右镜反。faded只褪色不能改变左右；其余形容词actual/distant/slight不表示影像翻转，其他项也非had been后的这个被动分词。
key帮助identify square as former mill，表示辨认图例。estimate不接as做身份判断；reach到达不表辨认；explore探索不提供X as Y认定结构；其他项不构成此原形识别动词。
several kilometres away及pale dot限定distant遥远。actual只表真实、slight微小不表距离；其余候选不在was后构成此表空间距离的形容词。
依据比例尺estimate distance估计距离。reach distance不等估算；identify可识别某距离而非按比例推算其长度，explore不表达数值估算；其余项不适合此原形计量动作。
spending time discovering where they went支持explore探索岔路。reach只是抵达，不能充分表述走访发现走向；estimate需要数值对象。identify在辨认路线语境有局部可行性，不能泛说语法不合法，但第6空图例辨认为identify X as Y，整组每项最多一次排除在第9空重复使用。其余候选不构成此原形探索动作。
actual position与只被proposed的点作事实/规划对比。distant只说明远近、slight不形容位置真伪、reversed为镜反照片非建筑位置；其余项不能作为此处真实位置的修饰。

He realised that the photograph had been (5) ____ from left to right when it was copied. The tiny words were mirror images too.

He found an unaltered copy in his notes. Its key helped him (6) ____ a black square as a former mill rather than a house. Owen decided to return another day to (9) ____ the side paths, spending time discovering where they went. Today he checked the mill's (10) ____ position carefully: a dotted square showed where a replacement had once been proposed, not where the old building stood.

completed_passage:
Owen was walking towards a fictional coastal village when he reached a fork. One branch of the path led downhill; the other climbed a ridge. The wooden sign was still there, but its painted letters had faded until almost nothing could be read. He hoped to reach the village before five, when his sister would meet him at its only bus stop.

A stone hut nearby offered shelter from a passing shower. Inside, Owen opened a photograph of an old map on his phone. Something seemed wrong: the river appeared on the opposite side of the road. He realised that the photograph had been reversed from left to right when it was copied. The tiny words were mirror images too.

He found an unaltered copy in his notes. Its key helped him identify a black square as a former mill rather than a house. Beyond it, a lighthouse was distant, appearing as a pale dot several kilometres away. The scale allowed him to estimate the remaining distance without measuring it on the ground.

Owen decided to return another day to explore the side paths, spending time discovering where they went. Today he checked the mill's actual position carefully: a dotted square showed where a replacement had once been proposed, not where the old building stood.
